Keywords: lockfile, pip freeze, poetry.lock, reproducible builds
Guidance: Installing from a loose requirements.txt (no pinned versions) means the same codebase can pull different transitive dependency versions on different days, breaking reproducibility.
Do: Use a lockfile (poetry.lock, pip-tools' requirements.txt, uv.lock) that pins exact versions including transitive deps.
Don't: Install dependencies from an unpinned requirements.txt in production.

Keywords: venv, virtualenv, global install, dependency conflict
Guidance: Installing packages into the system/global Python interpreter causes version conflicts between unrelated projects and can break OS-level tooling that depends on system Python.
Do: Create a project-scoped virtual environment (venv, poetry, uv) and never pip install into the system interpreter.
Don't: Run pip install directly against the system Python for application dependencies.

Guidance: Legacy setup.py-based packaging mixes build logic with arbitrary Python execution at install time; pyproject.toml with a declarative build backend is the modern, safer standard.
Do: Define package metadata and dependencies in pyproject.toml using a build backend like hatchling or setuptools' declarative mode.
Don't: Author new packages with a setup.py as the only packaging definition in 2026.

Keywords: asyncio, blocking call, event loop, sync in async
Guidance: A single synchronous blocking call (requests.get, time.sleep, sync DB driver) inside an async function stalls the entire event loop, silently killing concurrency for every other coroutine.
Do: Use async-native libraries (httpx, asyncpg) or run blocking calls in a thread pool via asyncio.to_thread.
Don't: Call a synchronous blocking library function directly inside an async def function.

Keywords: pytest fixture, fixture scope, test isolation, conftest
Guidance: A fixture scoped session/module when it holds mutable state can leak state between tests, causing order-dependent test failures that are hard to reproduce.
Do: Default fixtures to function scope; only widen scope (module/session) for genuinely expensive, immutable setup.
Don't: Share a mutable database connection or object across tests via a session-scoped fixture without resetting state.

Topic: Type hints and mypy in CI
Keywords: type hints, mypy, static typing, type checking
Guidance: Type hints with no enforcement (no mypy/pyright in CI) become stale documentation that silently drifts from the actual code, giving false confidence.
Do: Add type hints incrementally and run mypy/pyright in CI so hints stay accurate over time.
Don't: Add type hints once and never re-check them with a static type checker in CI.

Keywords: logging module, print debugging, log level, structured logging
Guidance: print() statements left in production code can't be filtered by severity, redirected, or correlated across requests the way the logging module's levels and handlers can.
Do: Use the logging module (or structlog) with appropriate levels, not print(), for anything beyond local debugging.
Don't: Leave print() statements as the primary diagnostic output in production services.

Keywords: mutable default argument, list default, shared state bug
Guidance: A mutable default argument (def f(items=[])) is evaluated once at function definition time and shared across every call, causing state to silently accumulate between unrelated calls.
Do: Use None as the default and initialize the mutable object inside the function body.
Don't: Use a mutable literal (list, dict, set) directly as a default argument value.
Example:
def add_item(item, items=None):
    items = items if items is not None else []
    items.append(item)
    return items

Keywords: dependency versioning, semver ranges, application pinning
Guidance: Libraries should specify loose compatible version ranges so they don't conflict with consumers' other dependencies, while applications should pin exact versions for reproducible deploys -- conflating the two causes dependency hell.
Do: Pin exact versions in application lockfiles; use loose compatible ranges (>=,<) in library package metadata.
Don't: Pin exact dependency versions in a published library's pyproject.toml.

Keywords: mocking, test doubles, integration test, flaky test
Guidance: Unit tests that make real network calls to external services are flaky (fail on network blips) and slow; they belong in a separate integration test suite, not the fast unit test loop.
Do: Mock/stub external service calls in unit tests; reserve real calls for a clearly separated integration test suite.
Don't: Let unit tests hit real third-party APIs or databases as part of the default fast test run.

Keywords: gil, global interpreter lock, multiprocessing, threading
Guidance: Using threading for CPU-bound work doesn't get real parallelism because of the GIL; only I/O-bound work benefits from threads, CPU-bound work needs multiprocessing or a native extension.
Do: Use multiprocessing (or a subinterpreter/native extension) for CPU-bound parallel work, threading/asyncio for I/O-bound concurrency.
Don't: Use threading expecting real parallel speedup on CPU-bound number crunching.
Example: from multiprocessing import Pool\nwith Pool(4) as p:\n    results = p.map(cpu_bound_fn, items)

Guidance: Unpickling data from an untrusted source (or eval()'ing user input) allows arbitrary code execution -- pickle is not a safe serialization format for anything crossing a trust boundary.
Do: Use JSON or another safe serialization format for untrusted input; never pickle.loads or eval() data from outside your trust boundary.
Don't: Deserialize user-supplied or network-received data with pickle.loads or eval().

Keywords: pip hash, requirements hash, supply chain security
Guidance: Installing from PyPI with no hash verification means a compromised or typosquatted package version can be installed silently even if the version pin looks correct.
Do: Use --require-hashes with pip-compiled requirements to verify package integrity at install time.
Don't: Install production dependencies with no hash verification.
